messages.author: b7832cf09ba80064
messages.subject: x-axis name problem
parts:
Hi,

i am trying to change the name of the axis in a ggplot. While for the
y axis a scale_y_continuous works fine, for the x-axis it does not.
The codefragment used is:

p <- ggplot() +
scale_y_continuous(name='b/a-ratio',limits=c(0.5,3.5)) +
geom_point(data=bs,aes(DoI,b.a.ratio,colour=Eye)) +
geom_line(data=bs,aes(DoI,b.a.ratio,colour=Eye)) +
facet_grid(. ~ PID)

DoI is a date within a range of 01-jan-2007 to 31-dec-2009.

Using scale_x_continuous with just the name (e.g. "scale_x_continuous
(name='Date of investigation')") results in the error: "Error: Non-
continuous variable supplied to scale_x_continuous."

How to set the limits for dates or how to set the axis name only?

Thanks in advance
Herbert

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: x-axis name problem
parts:
Hi Herbert -

At least two possible fixes.  One is the older scale_x_date('x title') and the other is the more recent (I think) change to xlab so that you can just do a + xlab('x title').

Cheers
david.

So both methods should work. However, why does the following code not
work?

p <- ggplot() +
labs(x="Date of investigation") +
scale_y_continuous(name=y_title,limits=c(0,120)) +
geom_point(data=bs,aes(DoI,X30Hz_A,colour=Eye)) +
geom_line(data=bs,aes(DoI,X30Hz_A,colour=Eye)) +

p <- ggplot() +
scale_x_date("Date of investigation") +
scale_y_continuous(name=y_title,limits=c(0,120)) +
geom_point(data=bs,aes(DoI,X30Hz_A,colour=Eye)) +
geom_line(data=bs,aes(DoI,X30Hz_A,colour=Eye)) +
facet_grid(. ~ PID)
theme_set(theme_bw())
p

Thanks
Herbert

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: x-axis name problem
parts:
On Sun, Apr 26, 2009 at 10:32 AM, Herbert Jägle
<herbert...@uni-tuebingen.de> wrote:
>
> So both methods should work. However, why does the following code not
> work?

Because you're using a non-standard construction - the following is
much to be preferred:

p <- ggplot(bs, aes(DoI, X30Hz_A,colour=Eye)) +

scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,120)) +
geom_point() +
geom_line() +
facet_grid(. ~ PID)

(it's also quite a bit shorter!)

The problem is in your code there's not enough information to figure
out what the x scale will be until just before the data is plotted,
and the way labs() works requires the scale to already be present
(this should be fixed in a future version).

Hadley
